doc.title: Last Straws: John Chaffe, Bris Jones, Bill Lee, Frank De La Houssaye, Bob Ice Interview, 1960-04-18

title: Chaffe's favorite musicians, banjoists and bands
summary: Chaffe favors the whole-band sound. He names Armstrong, King Oliver, George Lewis, the Dodds, St. Cyr and Jelly Roll Morton's Red Hot Peppers.

bands.name: Jelly Roll Morton's Red Hot Peppers

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Well, I don't really single them out, because I like the sound of a whole band rather than any one musician together. And I suppose if I had to pick any real favorites, of course, in the single musician field, I'd pick Louis Armstrong before 1930, and King Oliver and George Lewis and Baby Dodds and Johnny Dodds both.
Any banjo players? That's what I would like.

Well, I like St. Cyr's style a great deal. Of course, he's a six-string man. And I really like Blanche Murrow's style. It was very, very straight, but it certainly was tremendous in adding to the beat because the rest of the rhythm section worked the same way. I think it's very important to have a rhythm section for everybody working together.

Concentrate the same type of beat. As far as the whole band's concerned, I think that Jelly Roll Martin's Red Hot Peppers is the finest band that I had ever heard. However, there are several other bands which I have heard that I like very much, named with the New Orleans Feet Warmers, I believe, and the old Armstrong Hot 7, 1925-26 Hot 7.
